subject: MAP milestones & close timing — discount cadence + usage definitions
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@atlasretail.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: gus.romero@atlasretail.com
Date: 2027-03-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP proposal + target close window

Irene,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the batching suggestions. Attached is the draft MAP (Atlas_MAP_v2.xlsx) that lays out milestones, acceptance criteria for the pilot, and a proposed discount cadence tied to committed monthly throughput. High level asks from our side:

- 6-week pilot starting Apr 5, with milestone acceptance at week 4 (functionality + latency SLOs)
- If pilot passes, convert to a 12-month committed purchase (monthly committed tokens) with a tiered discount schedule that increases as we hit ramp milestones (25% at commit, +5% at 3mo, +5% at 6mo)
- Price protection: we want a 12-month floor on per-token pricing after conversion and an explicit true-up mechanism for usage over/under commit
- Need clarity on "what counts as usage" (generated tokens vs cached tokens, embeddings, reranking calls)

Two requests from procurement: a canonical definition of billable units and a draft clause that explains quarterly true-ups and whether credits or invoiced overages are used. Can you put us in touch with the team to align on contract language?

Appreciate it — attaching the MAP for your reference.

Samantha
Samantha Li
Head of AI Integrations, Atlas Retail
[Attachment: Atlas_MAP_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@atlasretail.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-24T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP proposal + target close window

Samantha — thanks, and great to hear the team's takeaways. We've reviewed Atlas_MAP_v2 and sketched an initial commercial response (attached: Redwood_MAP_response.docx). Key points up front:

- Pilot timing: we can start Apr 5 as long as the pilot model variant and dataset access are confirmed by Apr 1. Pilot acceptance at week 4 is fine, but we propose a short 72-hour acceptance period for latency/throughput verification to avoid indefinite open items.
- Commit & discounts: we can support a tiered discount cadence tied to committed monthly throughput. We prefer a model where the initial discount is applied to committed units only; ramp milestones unlock additional discounts prospectively (not retroactively).
- True-ups: Redwood typically executes quarterly true-ups where we reconcile committed units vs actual billable usage. We can do invoice-based overages or advance credit-based overages — willing to be flexible, but we need a clear waterfall: first apply unused committed units (carry-forward cap 1 quarter), then invoice overage at agreed rate.
- Price protection: we can offer a 12-month price protection window from the contract effective date. Outside that window, pricing may adjust with 30 days' notice but we will honor a floor tied to the committed rate.
- Definitions: important to align on exactly what counts as billable. Our proposed language in the response: billable usage = generated output tokens + embedding calls (counted per vector request) + active reranks; cached tokens (prefix repeated requests served entirely from KV cache) are excluded.

I'm looping Ben (sales lead on Atlas) and Marissa (revops/finance) to confirm billing mechanics and the language for the true-up clause. Can you confirm the pilot dataset schedule and whether you require sandbox VPC access? Also, any procurement deadlines we should be aware of for April?

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_MAP_response.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-30T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: internal: suggested redlines — true-up, price protection, usage defs

Irene / Marissa — quick internal note before we share negotiated language back to Atlas. Legal flagged two items: the proposed carry-forward cap and "prospective-only" discount accrual. I pushed back; the customer wants economic predictability. My recommended compromise below to include in the contract excerpt (we should post to the shared drive and attach a PDF redline):

1) True-up cadence: quarterly reconciliations. If actual billable usage > committed units, customer pays overage based on the committed per-unit rate for the overage tier; if actual < committed units, customer receives a credit equal to the difference, which can be applied to future invoices for up to one quarter (carry-forward cap = 1 quarter). Credits expire after the carry-forward period.

2) Price protection: 12-month protection on per-unit pricing starting on effective date. If Redwood reduces list prices within the protection window, Redwood will pass through the lower published list price to the customer; if Redwood raises prices, the committed per-unit rate is protected for 12 months. After 12 months, Redwood may adjust list prices with 30 days notice.

3) Definitions (we should be explicit):
   - Generated tokens: tokens produced by model at response time.
   - Embedding request: each API call that returns one or more vectors; billable as one unit per request multiplied by vector count (we can provide a multiplier table separately).
   - Reranking: counted per API call where full-text rerank is executed (not for cached score lookups).
   - Cached tokens: tokens served entirely from KV cache where no new inference occurs — excluded from billing.

4) Ramp discounts: discounts are applied prospectively on future committed units once a milestone is certified. No retroactive increases to previously invoiced amounts. However, to be accommodating, Redwood will apply a one-time credit equal to 50% of the incremental discount differential for the prior quarter (capped) to smooth invoicing at the first milestone catch-up. This is intended as a commercial compromise to keep numbers simple while protecting both parties.

Marissa — can you draft the redline snippet for section 4 (billing/true-up) and export a PDF excerpt (redlines_contract_excerpt.pdf) so we can send to Atlas. I want to present this as "reconciled compromise" rather than hard legal terms.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts
[Internal note: HubSpot pipeline ATL-2024-034]

From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@atlasretail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Gus Romero <gus.romero@atlasretail.com>, procurement@atlasretail.com
Date: 2027-04-12T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP milestones & close timing — discount cadence + usage definitions

Irene — thanks for the quick turnaround and Ben/Marissa for the compromise language. A few clarifying points from procurement and our legal team before we sign:

- The carry-forward cap of 1 quarter is acceptable, but procurement asks that credits be usable for up to 6 months (two quarters) in case our ramp is slower than expected. Can Redwood extend the carry-forward cap to 2 quarters?
- For price protection, we need explicit language that any change to how "embedded vector counting" is calculated requires 60 days' notice and an opportunity to re-negotiate if it increases effective pricing materially (>5% effective price movement).
- On the definition of cached tokens: please add a short test/example in the contract so there's no ambiguity (e.g., "if 80% of responses within a 24-hour window are served from identical KV cache state, those tokens are considered cached and excluded").

Assuming Redwood can accept the 2-quarter carry-forward and the 60-day notice for changes to vector-counting methodology, we can target signature for the 12-month committed contract by Apr 26 and hit the Apr 5 pilot start as planned. Procurement is also asking for a DocuSign link and the final redline PDF.

Samantha
Samantha Li
Head of AI Integrations, Atlas Retail
[Attachment: procurement_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)]
